hero.headline: SEC Proposes Eliminating Climate Disclosure Rule for Public Companies
hero.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed ending a regulation that would have required publicly traded companies to disclose whether they faced significant risks from climate change and its effects.

The regulation represented a comprehensive approach to climate-related financial disclosures. Under the proposed rule, all publicly traded companies would have been obligated to report on their exposure to climate-related risks and how those risks might affect their business operations and financial performance.

The SEC's move to eliminate the disclosure requirement marks a reversal in regulatory policy regarding corporate climate transparency. The commission's proposal would remove the obligation for companies to publicly report on their climate vulnerabilities.

Climate disclosure rules have been a topic of debate in corporate governance and environmental policy circles. Proponents of such regulations argue that investors need standardized information about climate risks to make informed decisions about their investments. Critics have raised concerns about the costs of compliance and the difficulty of quantifying climate-related risks.

The proposed elimination of the rule would affect thousands of publicly traded companies across all sectors of the economy. Companies in energy, manufacturing, agriculture, real estate, and financial services had been preparing to comply with the disclosure requirements.

The SEC's proposal follows broader discussions about the role of regulatory agencies in addressing climate change through corporate disclosure requirements. Financial regulators worldwide have taken varying approaches to climate risk disclosure, with some jurisdictions implementing mandatory reporting standards while others have adopted voluntary frameworks.

The commission will likely accept public comments on the proposal before making a final decision. Industry groups, environmental organizations, and investor coalitions are expected to submit feedback on the proposed rule change.

The fate of the climate disclosure requirement will affect how investors assess companies' exposure to physical risks from extreme weather events, transition risks from policy changes, and liability risks from climate-related litigation.

cards.headline: White House economic adviser predicts Strait of Hormuz will reopen soon
cards.teaser: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said oil shipments will pass through the Strait of Hormuz in one to two months.
cards.body:
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett predicted that oil shipments will pass through the Strait of Hormuz within one to two months. The strait has been closed amid the U.S.-Israeli conflict in Iran.

Hassett told a television interviewer that more traffic is now passing through the strait. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical passage for global oil shipments and has been disrupted during the conflict.

cards.headline: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: Israeli forces captured the Crusader-era fortress as part of an expanding ground offensive against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress in southern Lebanon that overlooks the border with Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the seizure as a "decisive shift" in the military campaign against Hezbollah, and the move suggests Israel intends an extended military presence in Lebanon.

The castle holds deep symbolic meaning for both nations. Israel previously occupied the site during its lengthy presence in southern Lebanon, and its recapture has revived difficult historical memories for both countries as the conflict with Hezbollah continues.

cards.headline: Zelensky hopes Trump envoys will visit Kyiv for talks
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he hopes White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will come to Kyiv in the coming weeks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he hopes White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law, will visit Kyiv for talks in the coming weeks. He was asked whether he had heard from the envoys and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

The Ukrainian president made the comments during an interview on a Sunday news program. Zelensky expressed interest in hosting the envoys for discussions about the ongoing situation in Ukraine.

cards.headline: US Military Helps 70 Commercial Ships Navigate Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: US Central Command has assisted roughly 70 commercial vessels through the strategic waterway over the past three weeks.
cards.body:
The US military has been quietly guiding commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route. According to a US Central Command official, approximately 70 commercial vessels have received assistance navigating the strait during the last three weeks.

The strait serves as a vital passage for international maritime trade, connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. The military's involvement in facilitating safe passage for commercial shipping reflects ongoing concerns about security in the region.

cards.headline: Brazil monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection
cards.teaser: If confirmed, the cases would mark the first Ebola infections outside Africa since the current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
Brazilian health authorities are investigating two suspected Ebola cases while awaiting test results. If confirmed, these would mark the first cases detected outside Africa since the outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The outbreak has so far remained confined to the African continent. Health officials are monitoring the Brazilian patients closely as investigations continue.

cards.headline: Newark mayor orders curfew around immigration detention center after clashes
cards.body:
Newark Mayor Ras Baraka imposed a mandatory curfew covering a half-mile area surrounding the Delaney Hall immigration detention facility following confrontations between protesters and New Jersey State Police. The restricted zone applies only to the immediate vicinity of the facility in New Jersey's largest city, rather than citywide.

The curfew was implemented after protesters and state police clashed outside Delaney Hall for a second consecutive night. The facility has been the focus of sustained demonstrations raising concerns about immigration detention policies and conditions.

Rep. Mikie Sherrill expressed support for the mayor's decision to establish the partial curfew. By limiting restrictions to the area directly around the detention center, local officials aimed to balance public safety with the right to protest.

Family visitation rights at the ICE facility were partially restored following one week of protests. The resumption of visiting privileges occurred as demonstrations continued outside the facility, with the resulting law enforcement confrontations prompting the curfew order.

The Delaney Hall facility houses immigration detainees in federal custody under Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations. The ongoing protests have drawn attention to both the conditions within the detention center and the policies governing how detainees are held.

The curfew reflects the mayor's effort to manage public safety concerns while demonstrations persist outside the facility. The mayor's office has not disclosed the duration of the curfew or specified what penalties violators will face.

The clashes between protesters and state police represent a significant escalation from the largely peaceful demonstrations that characterized the earlier part of the week. The deployment of New Jersey State Police indicates the extent of the law enforcement response mobilized in response to the protests.

Newark is home to approximately 311,000 residents, making it the most populous city in New Jersey. The location of the detention facility within city limits means local officials bear responsibility for managing the security situation surrounding the ongoing demonstrations.

The protests at Delaney Hall have highlighted broader concerns about immigration detention practices. By restoring family visitation while maintaining a perimeter curfew, officials attempted to address some grievances raised by demonstrators while containing potential public disorder.

The situation underscores the tension between protecting rights to assembly and demonstration against concerns about maintaining order and public safety during intense civic unrest. How local authorities balance these competing interests will likely shape the trajectory of future protests at the facility.

hero.headline: Blast at explosives storage building in Myanmar kills dozens
hero.body:
An explosion at a building storing mining explosives killed more than 45 people in a rebel-held village in northeast Myanmar near the Chinese border. Around 70 people were injured in the blast.

Insurgents said the explosion was caused by explosives being used for mining operations in the region. The building was located in an area controlled by rebel forces fighting the Myanmar military government.

Rescuers worked to recover victims from the site of the explosion. The blast occurred in a village in the northeast of the country, in territory held by opposition forces.

Myanmar has been in turmoil since the military seized power in 2021. Armed resistance groups control significant portions of the country, particularly in border regions. Fighting between the military and various insurgent groups has displaced hundreds of thousands of people.

The explosion adds to the humanitarian crisis in Myanmar, where ongoing conflict has strained medical services and emergency response capabilities in many areas. Rebel-held territories often lack adequate medical facilities to treat mass casualties.

The proximity to the Chinese border raises questions about the source and destination of the mining explosives. Myanmar's border regions have long been centers of both legal and illegal resource extraction, including jade, timber, and rare earth minerals.

Neither the Myanmar military government nor rebel groups have provided additional details about the circumstances of the explosion or whether it was accidental. The death toll may rise as rescue operations continue and more victims are recovered from the site.

cards.teaser: Israeli forces captured the Crusader-era fortress as part of an expanding ground offensive against Hezbollah.

Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress in southern Lebanon that overlooks the border with Israel. cards.headline: Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection
cards.teaser: If confirmed, the cases would mark the first Ebola infections outside Africa since the outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
Brazilian health authorities are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection. The individuals are undergoing tests to determine whether they have contracted the virus.

If confirmed, these would represent the first Ebola cases outside Africa since the current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested after Champions League riots in France
cards.teaser: Clashes with police left 219 people injured, including 57 officers.
cards.body:
Nearly 800 people were arrested following clashes with police at a Champions League match in France. The violence left 219 people injured, including 57 police officers.

Law enforcement deployed in significant numbers to manage the unrest, which represented one of the most serious incidents of football-related disorder in recent times.

cards.headline: Colombia holds presidential election
cards.teaser: Voters choose between the legacy of the country's first leftist leader, a far-right outsider, and a traditional conservative.
cards.body:
Colombians are casting ballots in the first round of a presidential election that serves as a referendum on outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro's policies. The vote comes a decade after the country signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), and candidates present starkly different visions for the nation's future and approach to peace.

The election takes place amid months of tension between President Petro and US counterpart Donald Trump over their differing political agendas. Voters are choosing between Petro's ally and pro-Trump candidates with competing ideological visions for Colombia's direction.

cards.headline: Dead whale towed to shore in Denmark for autopsy
cards.teaser: The whale, nicknamed Timmy, died despite multiple rescue attempts.
cards.body:
Authorities in Denmark brought the carcass of a humpback whale, nicknamed "Timmy" by German media, to shore for examination. The whale had been drifting near the Danish coast off Anholt for two weeks before being recovered.

Rescue efforts to save the whale ultimately proved unsuccessful before it died. Scientists will now conduct an autopsy to determine what caused the animal's death.

cards.headline: Trump calls for cancellation of Freedom 250 festival
cards.teaser: The president suggested holding a rally instead after most headliners dropped out of the White House-linked event.
cards.body:
President Trump called for the US Freedom 250 festival to be cancelled after most headlining performers withdrew from the White House-linked event. He suggested replacing it with a Make America Great Again rally instead.

Several artists dropped out of the festival, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride. The performers cited concerns that the event would be political in nature.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight to Spain returns to Newark over Bluetooth device
cards.teaser: A flight to Palma de Mallorca turned back to Newark after an onboard Bluetooth device raised security concerns.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Palma de Mallorca, Spain diverted back to Newark Liberty International Airport on Saturday evening. The aircraft turned around mid-flight after crew members identified a security concern related to a Bluetooth device onboard.

Air traffic audio and social media posts indicate that the name of the Bluetooth device prompted the security alert. Security personnel inspected the aircraft after it returned to Newark.

cards.headline: Pence calls Trump anti-weaponization fund deeply offensive
cards.teaser: The former vice president said he hopes the Trump administration will drop the $1.8 billion fund.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized a Trump administration fund as deeply offensive and called for it to be dropped. The fund, totaling $1.8 billion, is described as an anti-weaponization payout program.

Pence expressed hope that the Trump administration would abandon the fund. A list of potential applicants to the program has emerged, though Congress faces questions about what authority it has to limit or regulate the payments.

cards.headline: New York Mayor Mamdani to skip Israel parade, pledges police presence
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani will not attend the annual Israel Day Parade but has committed to a significant police deployment for the event.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will not attend the annual parade celebrating Israel, though he has committed to deploying a significant police presence at the event. The parade is set to take place amid declining American support for Israel.

Street closures are planned along the parade route in Manhattan for the celebration.

cards.headline: Officer seriously injured, shot fired after police car stolen in Northern Ireland
cards.teaser: A police officer in Northern Ireland was struck by a stolen police vehicle, and a shot was fired during the incident.
cards.body:
A Police Service of Northern Ireland officer sustained serious injuries after being struck by a stolen police car during an incident in which a shot was fired. Authorities responded to the incident, which represents a significant assault on law enforcement in the region.

A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder in connection with the attack.

cards.headline: Graham Platner's wife says she is disappointed sexting disclosure made public
cards.teaser: The wife of Senate candidate Graham Platner expressed anger after her past disclosure of his extramarital texts became public.
cards.body:
Graham Platner's wife expressed anger and disappointment that her earlier disclosure of his sexually explicit texting has become public. She had previously reported the messages to his Senate campaign while they were married.

The revelations have drawn scrutiny to Platner's Maine Senate bid. Senator Cory Booker said he has concerns about the candidate, stating that Platner "has questions to answer" and that campaigns provide a forum for addressing such matters.

cards.headline: China's Biotechnology Advances Raise Concerns About US Industry Leadership
cards.teaser: Clinical trials in China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotechnology sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials from Chinese pharmaceutical companies are drawing significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago. China's biotechnology sector has expanded considerably, prompting concerns among US industry observers about shifts in global drug development leadership.

The growth of China's biotech capabilities and clinical trial operations represents a notable change in the competitive landscape for pharmaceutical innovation. This development has raised questions about the sustainability of American dominance in research and drug development.

cards.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Earns $82 Million in Opening Weekend
cards.teaser: The low-budget horror movie from a 20-year-old filmmaker attracted strong turnout from young audiences at theaters.
cards.body:
Backrooms, a horror film that cost $10 million to produce, generated $82 million in ticket sales during its opening weekend. The movie was created by a 20-year-old filmmaker and drew substantial numbers of young moviegoers to theaters.

The film's performance adds to evidence that younger audiences will attend theatrical screenings when content appeals to their interests. The strong box office results for a relatively low-budget production demonstrate the continued viability of theatrical releases for certain types of films.

cards.headline: All-Electric Aircraft Completes Test Flight in New York City
cards.teaser: A new electric airplane conducted a demonstration flight, offering a look at potential changes to air travel technology.
cards.body:
An all-electric aircraft completed a test flight in New York City, showcasing emerging technology in aviation. The demonstration flight represents ongoing efforts to develop electric propulsion systems for passenger aircraft.

Electric aviation technology aims to reduce emissions from air travel by replacing traditional fuel-powered engines with battery-powered systems. The test flight in a major metropolitan area provided an opportunity to evaluate the aircraft's performance in real-world conditions.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Returns After Bluetooth Device Name Triggers Security Alert
cards.teaser: A United flight headed to Spain turned around after the crew was alerted to a Bluetooth network name that appeared threatening.
cards.body:
United Airlines Flight 236 from Newark to Palma de Mallorca turned back to its departure airport on Saturday night, about an hour after takeoff. The diversion was prompted by security concerns related to a Bluetooth device signal detected on the aircraft.

The flight crew repeatedly requested passengers to disable their Bluetooth devices after becoming aware of the potential threat. The aircraft was diverted back to Newark rather than continuing across the Atlantic to Spain.

cards.headline: Wall Street Discusses Potential SpaceX-Tesla Merger
cards.teaser: Investment analysts are examining the possibility of combining Elon Musk's aerospace and automotive companies.
cards.body:
Financial industry observers have begun discussing the prospect of a merger between SpaceX and Tesla, both controlled by Elon Musk. The speculation comes as SpaceX moves toward a potential public listing on the Nasdaq exchange.

A combination of the two companies could create an entity valued at approximately $3.4 trillion. Such a merger could also automatically trigger provisions in Musk's compensation package worth up to $1 trillion, according to financial analysts examining the scenario.

hero.headline: Apple plans smart glasses launch for late 2027
hero.body:
Apple is preparing to release consumer smart glasses in late 2027, according to reports from multiple technology publications. The product represents the company's entry into a market currently dominated by Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses.

The glasses are expected to incorporate artificial intelligence features and aim to disrupt the eyewear market in a manner similar to how the Apple Watch transformed the wearables category when it launched. Apple is reportedly developing the product to challenge existing privacy practices in the smart glasses industry.

The timeline places the smart glasses launch several years after Apple's Vision Pro headset, which the company released earlier. According to reports, Apple is also working on a lighter mixed reality headset called Vision Air, scheduled to arrive by 2029.

The late 2027 target date suggests Apple is taking time to develop the technology and features needed for a consumer-ready product. The company has historically entered product categories later than competitors but attempted to refine the user experience and integration with its ecosystem of devices.

Apple has not publicly confirmed the smart glasses project or provided details about features, pricing, or technical specifications. The reports indicate the company sees the glasses as a significant new product category that could expand its wearables business beyond watches and headphones.

The launch timing would give Apple several years to observe how competitors navigate privacy concerns and consumer adoption challenges in the smart glasses market. Meta has faced scrutiny over how its Ray-Ban smart glasses handle recording and data collection in public spaces.

Industry observers expect Apple to emphasize privacy protections and user controls in its approach to smart glasses, consistent with the company's marketing positioning in other product categories. The success of the product will likely depend on factors including battery life, design, functionality, and how well the glasses integrate with iPhones and other Apple devices.

cards.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches in October with Korean war setting
cards.teaser: The next installment in the Call of Duty franchise will release on October 23 with a campaign set during a present-day Korean conflict.
cards.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 on Nintendo Switch 2 for the first time. The game includes campaign, multiplayer, and a DMZ mode at launch.

The campaign depicts a present-day conflict on the Korean peninsula, marking a return to the series' history of real-world controversy. Infinity Ward has positioned the game as grounded in military authenticity, aiming for a more authentic and transparent shooter experience. The setting represents a notable shift from recent entries that favored melodrama over gritty realism.

cards.headline: Chinese startup successfully tests reusable rocket engine
cards.teaser: Mega Engine Technology, founded in 2024 by an MIT graduate, has advanced development of a high-pressure oxygen-rich staged-combustion engine.
cards.body:
Mega Engine Technology, a Chinese startup co-founded by Zhang Chenxing in early 2024, has successfully fired a reusable staged-combustion rocket engine. Zhang holds a doctorate from MIT and established the company in Xi'an.

The technology uses high-pressure oxygen-rich staged-combustion, an approach that previously existed almost entirely within Chinese state propulsion facilities. The engine is designed to compete with SpaceX technology and enable deep space missions. The company achieved the milestone test by May 2026, less than two years after its founding.

cards.headline: Artist reaches agreement with AI startup over meme use
cards.teaser: KC Green, creator of the "This is fine" meme, has settled a dispute with Artisan after the startup used his work in advertising.
cards.body:
KC Green, the artist behind the widely recognized "This is fine" meme, has reached an agreement with AI startup Artisan. The startup had used Green's meme in advertisements without authorization.

Artisan has taken down the ads featuring the "This is fine" image following the agreement. The meme, which depicts a dog sitting calmly in a burning room, has become a popular internet symbol for accepting dire situations.

cards.headline: Black founders secure highest quarterly funding since 2022
cards.teaser: Venture capital investment in Black-led startups reached a two-year high in the most recent quarter, according to Crunchbase data.
cards.body:
Black founders reached their highest quarterly funding level since 2022, according to Crunchbase research. The uptick suggests a potential shift in how venture capital is being allocated.

However, significant barriers persist. Gené Teare, Crunchbase's head of research, points to persistent challenges including limited access to investor networks, professional relationships, and early introductions—structural obstacles that continue to impede sustained funding growth for Black entrepreneurs.

cards.headline: Two weekend box office leaders both directed by former YouTubers
cards.teaser: The top two films at the box office were both made by directors who started their careers creating content on YouTube.
cards.body:
The two highest-grossing movies over the weekend were directed by filmmakers who began as YouTube content creators. Both films fall within the horror genre, suggesting a pipeline from online video creation to theatrical releases.

The success of both films demonstrates how YouTube has become a pathway for directors to transition into traditional filmmaking. The weekend results indicate audiences are responding positively to projects from creators who built followings through online platforms before moving into feature film production.

cards.headline: Apple plans new Apple TV and HomePod mini for fall release
cards.teaser: Updated versions of Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini are reportedly ready to launch, with a possible refresh of the Siri Remote.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing to release new versions of its Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini devices this fall, according to reports. The products are described as nearly ready for launch.

A refreshed Siri Remote is also possible as part of the updates. The timing appears linked to planned improvements to Siri, Apple's voice assistant. The Apple TV 4K update would break a record for the longest gap between releases in the product line's history.

hero.headline: Ball State freshman football player Gavin Yates-Lyons dies at 18
hero.body:
The university confirmed the death of Yates-Lyons, who had joined the Cardinals football program as a member of the incoming freshman class. He played the defensive back position.

No further details about the circumstances of his death were provided by the university or the athletic department. The loss affects the Ball State football community as the team prepares for the upcoming season.

Yates-Lyons was among the newest members of the Ball State football roster, having recently arrived on campus to begin his college football career. The defensive back had been part of the team's recruiting class.

The death of a college athlete at such a young age represents a significant loss for the Ball State community. Universities typically provide support services for students and staff members affected by such tragedies.

Ball State University is located in Muncie, Indiana, and competes in the Mid-American Conference. The football program will now move forward without Yates-Lyons as part of its roster.

The Cardinals football team had been preparing for the upcoming season with Yates-Lyons expected to contribute to the defensive backfield. His death comes during what would have been his first year with the program.

College football programs across the country face occasional tragedies involving student-athletes. The death of a freshman player affects not only the immediate team but also the broader university community and the player's family and friends.

cards.headline: Blue Jays outfielder Jesus Sanchez injured by ball thrown from stands
cards.teaser: Jesus Sanchez left the game against Baltimore after being hit on the wrist by a ball thrown by a fan.
cards.body:
Blue Jays outfielder Jesus Sanchez was forced to leave Sunday's game against the Orioles after being struck on the wrist by a ball thrown from the stands. The incident occurred during the matchup between Toronto and Baltimore at the ballpark.

The injury prompted Sanchez's removal from the game. The exact circumstances surrounding the thrown ball and the extent of Sanchez's wrist injury were not detailed in available reports.

cards.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander calls MVP season a failure after Thunder elimination
cards.teaser: The two-time MVP said his season fell short after Oklahoma City was eliminated before defending their NBA Finals title.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander won his second consecutive MVP award, but he's not celebrating. The Thunder guard called his season a failure after Oklahoma City was eliminated from the playoffs before reaching the NBA Finals, ending their chance to defend their championship title.

The reigning champion Thunder fell to the San Antonio Spurs in a competitive Western Conference Finals series, with Game 7 deciding their fate. Despite individual accolades, Gilgeous-Alexander's accomplishments were overshadowed by the team's postseason disappointment.

cards.headline: Norway wins first ice hockey world championship medal with overtime upset of Canada
cards.teaser: Norway defeated Canada 3-2 in overtime to capture bronze at the world championship.
cards.body:
Norway secured its first ice hockey world championship medal in dramatic fashion, defeating Canada 3-2 in overtime of the bronze medal game. The match was tightly contested, with both teams tied 2-2 at the end of regulation before Norway found the back of the net in the extra period.

The victory marks a historic milestone for the Norwegian national team on the world championship stage. Canada, traditionally one of the sport's elite nations, was unable to claim the bronze medal in the upset result.

cards.headline: Iga Swiatek eliminated from French Open as all defending champions exit
cards.teaser: Four-time champion Swiatek lost to Marta Kostyuk, who advanced to her first French Open quarterfinal.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk defeated four-time French Open champion Iga Swiatek in the fourth round, advancing to the quarterfinals for the first time in her career. The upset marked a significant moment in the tournament as Swiatek's title defense came to an end.

Kostyuk's victory completed the elimination of all defending singles champions from the French Open, capping a notable run of upsets in the tournament.

cards.headline: South Africa's World Cup arrival delayed by visa problems
cards.teaser: The team's flight from Johannesburg to Mexico was rebooked after visa issues caused delays.
cards.body:
South Africa's World Cup flight has been delayed due to visa issues. The team's departure from Johannesburg's OR Tambo International Airport to Mexico was originally scheduled to arrive on Sunday morning but has been rescheduled for Monday morning, according to the South African Football Association.

The squad was heading to Mexico for their opening match of the FIFA World Cup.

cards.headline: Knicks draw nearly half of all NBA Finals bets at DraftKings
cards.teaser: New York has attracted close to 50% of all money wagered on the championship winner this season.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks have attracted nearly half of all money wagered on the NBA Finals winner at DraftKings Sportsbook in New York. Their betting volume is almost as large as every other team combined.

The Knicks will face the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals after the Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals. Victor Wembanyama scored 22 points to lead San Antonio to victory. Game 1 is scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

hero.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Opens With $82 Million at Box Office
hero.body:
The horror film Backrooms earned $82 million in its opening weekend, powered by young moviegoers. The film marks the box office debut for director Kane Parsons, who previously built an audience on YouTube.

Parsons becomes the youngest filmmaker to reach the number one spot at the box office. The film's opening weekend performance represents a significant achievement for the horror genre and for directors who emerged from online platforms.

Backrooms joins Obsession as part of what observers are calling a horror renaissance aimed at younger audiences. Both films this weekend were directed by filmmakers who started on YouTube, marking a shift in how studio films are being made.

Obsession, directed by Curry Barker, also performed well in its third weekend. The film saw an unprecedented jump in ticket sales, continuing its strong performance since opening.

The Mandalorian and Grogu experienced a 70 percent drop in its second weekend, falling behind the new horror release. The Star Wars spinoff had opened strong the previous weekend but could not maintain momentum against the new competition.

Backrooms is based on an internet horror concept that originated online and built a following before being adapted for theaters. The film's success suggests that studios are finding new talent and intellectual property from digital creators.

Parsons' background as a YouTube content creator gave him experience in visual storytelling and building an audience, skills that translated to traditional filmmaking. His transition from online content to theatrical release represents a pathway that other digital creators may follow.

The strong opening demonstrates that younger audiences remain willing to see films in theaters when the content appeals to them. Horror films have consistently performed well with this demographic, and Backrooms capitalized on existing online awareness of the concept.

The film's performance will likely encourage studios to continue seeking projects from digital creators and adapting internet-native concepts for theatrical release.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa Marries Callum Turner in London
cards.teaser: The singer and actor held a private ceremony at Old Marylebone Town Hall.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa married actor Callum Turner during a private ceremony in London on Sunday. The wedding took place at Old Marylebone Town Hall.

The couple kept the event intimate, with details about attendees and the ceremony not publicly disclosed. Both Lipa and Turner have maintained relatively private personal lives despite their public careers.

cards.headline: Ronald LaPread, Commodores Co-Founder, Dies at 75
cards.teaser: The bassist and founding member of the Commodores died in Auckland, where he had lived for 40 years.
cards.body:
Ronald LaPread, co-founding member and former bassist of the Commodores, died at age 75. He died in Auckland, New Zealand, where he had lived for four decades.

LaPread helped establish the Commodores, the funk and soul group that produced hits including "Brick House" and "Easy." The band achieved major commercial success in the 1970s and 1980s, and LaPread's bass work was integral to their sound.

cards.headline: KSI Leaves Sidemen After 13 Years
cards.teaser: The YouTuber, whose real name is Olajide Olatunji, has been part of the group since 2013.
cards.body:
KSI has left the Sidemen, the YouTube collective he joined in 2013. The creator, whose real name is Olajide Olatunji, announced his departure after 13 years with the group.

The Sidemen became one of the most popular YouTube collectives, producing videos and building a business empire around their content. KSI's departure marks a significant change for the group, which has maintained its core membership for over a decade.

cards.headline: Trump Calls for Cancellation of Freedom 250 Concert After Artist Withdrawals
cards.teaser: Multiple performers dropped out of the Washington event after learning about organizers' connections to Trump.
cards.body:
Several high-profile performers withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series after discovering the event's connection to Trump. Young MC, Martina McBride, and Bret Michaels announced they would not participate, citing concerns that the Washington, D.C. event would become politicized.

Trump responded by calling for the concert's cancellation and dismissing the departing artists' music as boring. He suggested holding a "Make America Great Again" rally as an alternative celebration for America's 250th anniversary.

cards.headline: Cody Rhodes Defeats Gunther at WWE Clash in Italy
cards.teaser: Rhodes retained his WWE Championship in the main event of the Italian pay-per-view.
cards.body:
Cody Rhodes defeated Gunther at WWE Clash in Italy to retain the WWE Championship. The match headlined the event held in Italy on Sunday.

The event also featured Roman Reigns facing Jacob Fatu in a Tribal Combat match, and Oba Femi competing against Brock Lesnar. The show marked WWE's latest international pay-per-view event.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Delivers Freestyle Targeting Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj
cards.teaser: The rapper performed a surprise a cappella freestyle at the Roots Picnic festival.
cards.body:
Jay-Z performed a surprise a cappella freestyle at the Roots Picnic on Saturday that included disses aimed at Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj. The performance was unannounced and caught attendees off guard.

The rapper delivered the freestyle without instrumental backing, using only his voice. The Roots Picnic, an annual music festival in Philadelphia, has featured surprise performances from major artists in previous years.

hero.headline: RNC to hold midterm convention before general election
hero.teaser: Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters said the party will hold a midterm convention as President Trump outlined last September.
hero.body:
Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters confirmed the party will proceed with a midterm convention before the general election. Trump outlined the plan last September.

Gruters described a tight timeline for the event. "There's a very short window of doing it after the last primary ballots have been cast and before the general election," he said. He confirmed the party is moving forward with the plans.

cards.headline: Senator says Iran stronger than before war began three months ago
cards.teaser: Sen.
cards.body:
Sen. Chris Coons said Iran has grown stronger since the U.S. war with the country began three months ago. "Frankly, Iran is stronger than they were 90 days ago, before this war, because they've used their cheap and lethal drones, not just to close the Strait of Hormuz, but also to project power," the Delaware Democrat said during a television interview.

The conflict has driven up U.S. inflation to its fastest pace in three years, with energy prices surging amid the war. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, has disrupted markets and eroded household purchasing power. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett predicted oil shipments will resume through the strait within one to two months.

cards.headline: Booker says Maine Senate candidate has questions to answer
cards.teaser: Sen. Cory Booker said Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner must address reports of sexually explicit messages with multiple women.
cards.body:
Sen. Cory Booker expressed concerns about Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner's campaign following reports that Platner sent sexually explicit messages to multiple women while married. In an appearance on ABC's This Week, Booker said Platner "has questions to answer" and suggested the campaign process would be the appropriate venue for addressing the revelations.

Booker, a New Jersey Democrat, indicated that the controversy could affect Democratic prospects in the Maine Senate race, where Platner is running as the party's candidate.

cards.headline: GOP strategist calls Trump backing of Paxton a costly mistake
cards.teaser: Republican strategist Brad Todd said President Trump made a major error by endorsing Ken Paxton over John Cornyn in the Texas Senate race.
cards.body:
GOP strategist Brad Todd said President Trump made a $100 million mistake by backing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton to replace Sen. John Cornyn. Todd criticized the president's decision to urge Republican primary voters to support Paxton over the incumbent senator.

Todd said Cornyn would have been a stronger candidate than Paxton. The assessment comes after Paxton won his primary runoff and will face state Rep. James Talarico in the general election.

cards.headline: Beshear says Democrats can win Texas Senate seat after Paxton primary victory
cards.teaser: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said Democrats have a chance to win in Texas after Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff.
cards.body:
Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said Democrats have a chance at winning a Senate seat in Texas following Attorney General Ken Paxton's recent runoff victory. Beshear indicated that "Texas is in play" for Democrats following the Republican primary outcome.

Paxton will advance to face his Democratic opponent in the general election. Democrats have not won a statewide Senate seat in Texas for more than 30 years.

cards.headline: Zelensky hopes Trump envoys will visit Kyiv for talks
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he hopes White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will come to Kyiv in the coming weeks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he hopes White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law, will visit Kyiv for talks in the coming weeks. He was asked whether he had heard from the envoys and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

The Ukrainian president made the comments during an interview on a Sunday news program. Zelensky expressed interest in hosting the envoys for discussions about the ongoing situation in Ukraine.

cards.headline: White House economic adviser predicts Strait of Hormuz will reopen soon
cards.teaser: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said oil shipments will pass through the Strait of Hormuz in one to two months.
cards.body:
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett predicted that oil shipments will pass through the Strait of Hormuz within one to two months. The strait has been closed amid the U.S.-Israeli conflict in Iran.

Hassett told a television interviewer that more traffic is now passing through the strait. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical passage for global oil shipments and has been disrupted during the conflict.
